bull_bear.body:
- IPO ~INR31.39 cr raised (Dec-2025 SME listing); ~99.5% deployed per objects, ~INR15-20 lakh pending.
- Debt ~INR4 cr (up from ~INR0.5 cr) — majority promoter loans, plus one bank loan @9.5% / 8-yr.
- RSVP Infotech bolt-on ~INR0.98 cr (Mar-2026). No dividend mentioned (recently listed micro-cap reinvesting).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Not a manufacturer:** robots OEM-contracted in India + imported from China → margin/supply/FX/tariff & differentiation risk; "proprietary" IP still nascent (TRN just formed).
- **Working capital / receivables stretch:** AV-SITC billing only on commissioning; project cycles slip on client side; receivables spike each H2. Mgmt says no sticky debtors but it's a structural drag.
- **H2 concentration / lumpiness:** revenue heavily back-ended to Q3/Q4 (project deliveries) — quarterly volatility.
- **Geographic concentration:** heavy Gujarat reliance; diversification (metros + UAE) just starting.
- **Single-voice, micro-cap SME:** only the MD on the call; low float/liquidity; aggressive ~50% growth + margin guidance hard to verify; some OCR/number inconsistencies in the transcript.
- **Promoter-funded debt** rising; governance/related-party watch.
- **Execution on RSVP/UAE/TRN** all unproven (FY27 contributions are projections).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - MD candid and accessible (16 yrs AV/IT background; ex-TE Connectivity, Kramer Electronics). Answered margin, WC, sourcing, acquisition-cost questions directly. Tone is confident-promotional, typical of a freshly-listed SME founder; heavy use of "we are seeing lots of trends." Guidance is broad-brush (40-50% growth, +2-3% margin) without granular bridges; the convergence/TAM framing ($107bn global service robotics by 2030) is top-down. No CFO/independent voice on the call — a quality/oversight gap to monitor.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The entire margin and re-rating story rests on a **mix-shift, not a manufacturing edge** — Nanta buys robots (India OEM + China imports) and wraps them in software/integration; durable advantage depends on TRN actually building proprietary product, which has barely started.
- The eye-catching "EBITDA INR84 crores" in H2 is an OCR/transcript error; real figure ~INR8.4 cr (17.3% of INR48.6 cr) — don't propagate the headline.
- RSVP Infotech (INR0.98 cr) is positioned to add INR15-20 cr revenue in FY27 — a ~15-20x revenue-to-cost ambition that is the single biggest swing factor in the ~50% growth guide; verify next quarter.
- Receivables/WC are the real risk, not demand: INR35 cr of H2's INR48 cr already collected, so cash conversion is okay so far, but the AV-SITC commissioning lag structurally inflates the balance sheet each H2.
- This is a sub-INR100 cr revenue, ~INR300 cr-mcap BSE-SME — interesting as a thematic India-robotics/AI-adoption proxy, but liquidity, disclosure depth, and founder-only governance make it speculative.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- IPO proceeds are earmarked specifically for the Experience Centre buildout; the company completed its BSE SME listing in December 2025.
- Company discloses that FY26 ROE/ROCE are computed on a post-listing equity base and capital-employed structure, while FY24-FY25 reflect the pre-listing base — flagged by management as the reason for the ROE/ROCE decline, i.e. an equity-dilution effect from the IPO rather than an operating deterioration.
- Growth capital has been directed into the RSVP Infotech acquisition and Experience Centre infrastructure rather than shareholder distributions; no dividend policy is mentioned in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Comprehensive, end-to-end AV integration offering spanning system design, integration and management and on-site support, so a single vendor covers the full deployment
- Breadth of the distributed AV product range - LED screens, professional displays, digital signage, digital podiums, video conferencing and UC devices plus accessories
- Proprietary AI platforms NTalk and NTRA launched during the year, and a branded service-robot line (Albotix) with over 400 robots sold
- Management states that experience in this business and quality assurance are the basis for overcoming competition, and that there are not enough competitors offering services like theirs
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Complex global supply chain — Management flags that companies have to juggle internal and external resources while staying within international standards, and that issues such as traceability and compliance are increasing operational burdens.
- Uncertain and cyclical demand — Economic volatility and cyclical demand cause fluctuations in production, and shifts in consumer preference can spike demand for an individual product; efficient lean capabilities must be in place to keep inventory aligned with demand.
- Competition from better-resourced and unorganised players — The company operates in a competitive atmosphere in which some competitors may have greater resources than those available to it, and it faces competition from both organised and unorganised players.
- Price-led buying decisions — Although product quality, brand value and distribution network are key factors in client decisions, management states price is the deciding factor in most cases - a structural constraint on pricing power and margin.
- Dependence on client relationships and reputation — Management identifies client relationships, reputation and the relative quality and price of the services as the principal factors affecting competition in its business, making the franchise reliant on intangibles rather than contracted capacity.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Robotics & AI (Albotix brand; ~36-37% of FY26 revenue):** service robots across hospitality (largest — hotels, restaurants, large hospitals, FM premises), then manufacturing & government. Emerging demand: outdoor cleaning robots, reception robots, warehousing robots. Robots are **manufactured by third-party OEMs in India under contract, plus some directly imported from China** — Nanta is not a robot manufacturer; it's a brand/solution integrator.
- **AI & Software:** proprietary platforms NTalk and NTRA (conversational AI, predictive analytics, enterprise software, intelligent workflow). Augmented by RSVP Infotech acquisition (team + clients).
- **Audio-Visual (AV):** end-to-end SITC integration (design, supply, install, test, commission, maintenance) for enterprise/institutional/government. Lower margin, project-cycle-dependent, the main working-capital drag.
- **Subsidiaries:** TRN — The Robotics Nexus (51% Nanta-owned) = new dedicated R&D vehicle for robotics/AI/automation; Nanta Technologies FZ LLC (UAE, wholly-owned) = GCC gateway (UAE, Saudi, Qatar, Kuwait).
- **Marquee clients cited:** Adani, IFFCO, Indian Hotels (IHCL), HAL, ISRO, BARC, Gujarat Electricity Authority, L&T, Indian Coast Guard, Red Cross.

business.body:
- Integrated player across two verticals, Robotics & AI Solutions and Audio-Visual (AV) Solutions, combining hardware deployment with software and AI-driven capabilities.
- Describes itself as well-positioned to benefit from rising industrial-automation demand across construction, manufacturing, logistics and real estate, and from Al-driven government and digital-initiative tailwinds.
- Promoter-led leadership: Mayank Jani (Managing Director, 16+ years AV/IT industry experience, ex-TE Connectivity and Kramer Electronics) and Mansiben Jani (Chairman & Whole-Time Director, co-founder of predecessor MNT Technologies since 2018).
- Strategic Technology Acquisition (RSVP Infotech) is cited as a distinct business strength, strengthening AI and software capabilities and the Allbotix robotics/automation technology architecture.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] RSVP Infotech acquired during FY26, adding 14 AI engineers and strengthening AI/software capabilities, the Allbotix platform architecture, and enterprise engagement capabilities for larger automation deployments.
- [Corporate history] Nanta Tech Limited incorporated June 2023; acquired the business of proprietorship-founded (2018) MNT Technologies on a going-concern basis in February 2024; listed on the BSE SME platform in December 2025.
- [Market tailwinds cited by company] Indian robotics market sized at $1.98bn (2025) growing to a projected $7.38bn (2034P); India ranked 6th globally in robot installations with cited 32x headroom versus China at similar population; robot component prices cited as down ~60% between 2022-2025, improving deployment ROI; Indian robotics startup funding cited as growing from $28.8M (2022) to $117M (2024).

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** ~50% (also stated as "40-50%" overall operations growth).
- **Margin:** EBITDA margin to expand a further ~2-3% pts in FY27 (driven by rising robotics/AI mix).
- **Robotics & AI mix:** rise from ~36-37% of FY26 revenue toward ~60-65% in FY27 (mgmt expects this segment to "double").
- **UAE subsidiary:** revenue from Q2 FY27 (India Q2); FY27 target ~USD2m (~INR30 cr). Setup cost ~INR20-25 lakh.
- **RSVP Infotech:** ~INR15-20 cr of business in FY27 from RSVP's existing clients (served under Nanta).
- **R&D (via TRN):** ~INR2-3 cr FY27 (up to INR5 cr if more projects), vs only ~INR35-40 lakh last year; already baked into the margin guidance.
- **Dealers/distributors:** grow from 4 today to ≥15 by FY27-end (UAE + India metros — Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Chennai).
- **Working capital:** expected to trend down (robotics/AI is more B2C, less heavy-project execution).
- **Experience Center (IPO-funded):** ~95% built, opening "very soon."

outlook.body:

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion in this year was corporate and footprint-led rather than plant-led. The Company completed its Initial Public Offer, allotting 14,46,000 equity shares at Rs. 220 per share on 29th December 2025 under a shareholder authorisation for an issue of up to Rs. 50 Crore, and the Chairman describes the year as one in which the company transitioned from blueprint to reality, delivering on the strategic promises made following the IPO. Subsequent to the year end, the Company reported that development of its flagship Experience Center was near-complete, and it set up two new entities to extend reach and capability: Nanta Technologies FZ-LLC in the UAE, incorporated on April 23, 2026 to drive GCC market entry, and TRN India Private Limited, incorporated on April 24, 2026 to strengthen R&D in robotics and automation. No manufacturing capacity, plant or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material; the capital-commitments note supplied here carries the caption 'Estimated Amount of Contracts Remaining to be Executed on Capital Account and not Provided for' but no attributable figure or period.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Changing economic and business conditions, rapid technology innovation and adoption and globalisation are creating an increasingly competitive market environment that drives corporations to transform the manner in which they operate; companies are focusing more on revenue growth, profitability and asset efficiency
- Growth in the Indian economy and demand is said to create unprecedented opportunities for the company to invest in its core businesses, with the outlook for the overall industries described as positive
- Continual growth in this sector in India is seen as necessary to support the industry, and the company says it is making all effort to accelerate the growth of its business
- Stated demand opportunities: vast industrial presence in both public and private sectors, huge demand for domestic services, availability of low-cost skilled human resources, and continued government thrust on reforms and further liberalisation
- Price is the deciding factor in most client decisions, alongside product quality, brand value and distribution network - a margin constraint management explicitly acknowledges
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Nanta Tech is a tiny (~INR70 cr revenue) Ahmedabad-based BSE-SME systems integrator pivoting from low-margin project-based Audio-Visual integration toward higher-margin service robotics (Albotix) and AI/software, fresh off a Dec-2025 SME IPO (~INR31.4 cr raised, ~99.5% deployed). FY26 revenue +36.8% to INR70.1 cr with PAT +70.5% to INR8.2 cr as the Robotics & AI mix rose to ~36-37% of revenue (mgmt targets ~60-65% in FY27) and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.4%. The growth case (UAE/GCC entry, RSVP AI acquisition, TRN R&D arm, ~50% FY27 revenue guidance) is real but early, sourcing-dependent (robots OEM/China-sourced, not self-made), heavily H2-skewed, and carries stretched working-capital/receivables typical of project SITC business.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Nanta Tech Limited is an Ahmedabad-based provider of end-to-end audio-visual integration and AV product distribution, which also sells service robots and software development services, listed on the BSE SME Platform of BSE Limited since December 31, 2025.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is engaged in the business of Audio Visual (AV) integration, supply and distribution of AV Products, Service Robots and Software Development related services. It provides comprehensive, end-to-end AV integration solutions covering system design, integration and management and on-site support. In addition, it is actively involved in the direct selling and distribution of a wide range of AV products to public- and private-sector customers.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Robotics & AI (Albotix brand; ~36-37% of FY26 revenue):** service robots across hospitality (largest — hotels, restaurants, large hospitals, FM premises), then manufacturing & government. Emerging demand: outdoor cleaning robots, reception robots, warehousing robots. Robots are **manufactured by third-party OEMs in India under contract, plus some directly imported from China** — Nanta is not a robot manufacturer; it's a brand/solution integrator.
- **AI & Software:** proprietary platforms NTalk and NTRA (conversational AI, predictive analytics, enterprise software, intelligent workflow). Augmented by RSVP Infotech acquisition (team + clients).
- **Audio-Visual (AV):** end-to-end SITC integration (design, supply, install, test, commission, maintenance) for enterprise/institutional/government. Lower margin, project-cycle-dependent, the main working-capital drag.
- **Subsidiaries:** TRN — The Robotics Nexus (51% Nanta-owned) = new dedicated R&D vehicle for robotics/AI/automation; Nanta Technologies FZ LLC (UAE, wholly-owned) = GCC gateway (UAE, Saudi, Qatar, Kuwait).
- **Marquee clients cited:** Adani, IFFCO, Indian Hotels (IHCL), HAL, ISRO, BARC, Gujarat Electricity Authority, L&T, Indian Coast Guard, Red Cross.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **AV Integration Services:** System design, Integration and management, On-site support
- **AV Products (direct selling and distribution):** Indoor and outdoor active LED screens, Professional display screens (touch and non-touch), Digital signage displays, Digital podiums, Video conferencing cameras, Processors, Media players, Speakers, Microphones, Amplifiers, Unified communication (UC) devices, Mounts, cables and other related accessories
- **Service Robots:** Albotix
- **Software Development / AI platforms:** NTalk, NTRA

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India - domestic market
- GCC market, targeted through the newly incorporated UAE entity Nanta Technologies FZ-LLC

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- No formal order book disclosed (project + product business). Notable recent win: **INR6.6 cr AI-automation order from Pointer Insurance Broker Pvt Ltd** (AI chatbot, predictive analytics, intelligent workflow) — flagged as a BFSI-segment entry.
- ~400 robots deployed/sold in FY26 (cumulative operational milestone).
- Pipeline drivers: UAE/GCC inquiries & POCs (UAE base already exists, not from zero); dealer network expansion; Experience Center to drive proof-of-concept conversions.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth FY27:** ~50% (also stated as "40-50%" overall operations growth).
- **Margin:** EBITDA margin to expand a further ~2-3% pts in FY27 (driven by rising robotics/AI mix).
- **Robotics & AI mix:** rise from ~36-37% of FY26 revenue toward ~60-65% in FY27 (mgmt expects this segment to "double").
- **UAE subsidiary:** revenue from Q2 FY27 (India Q2); FY27 target ~USD2m (~INR30 cr). Setup cost ~INR20-25 lakh.
- **RSVP Infotech:** ~INR15-20 cr of business in FY27 from RSVP's existing clients (served under Nanta).
- **R&D (via TRN):** ~INR2-3 cr FY27 (up to INR5 cr if more projects), vs only ~INR35-40 lakh last year; already baked into the margin guidance.
- **Dealers/distributors:** grow from 4 today to ≥15 by FY27-end (UAE + India metros — Mumbai, Bangalore, Delhi, Chennai).
- **Working capital:** expected to trend down (robotics/AI is more B2C, less heavy-project execution).
- **Experience Center (IPO-funded):** ~95% built, opening "very soon."

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **GCC/UAE expansion** via FZ LLC — full end-to-end robotics+software solution as the differentiator vs local/global peers; ~INR30 cr FY27 target.
- **BFSI AI automation** — Pointer Insurance win positioned as a beachhead in a "substantial" segment.
- **Robotics category broadening** — from hospitality into cleaning (outdoor), reception, warehousing/manufacturing.
- **TRN R&D arm** — new-product/new-model development to build proprietary IP (currently OEM/imported).
- **Dealer/distribution scale-up** (4 → 15) with target-based incentive program + roadshows across metros.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Changing economic and business conditions, rapid technology innovation and adoption and globalisation are creating an increasingly competitive market environment that drives corporations to transform the manner in which they operate; companies are focusing more on revenue growth, profitability and asset efficiency
- Growth in the Indian economy and demand is said to create unprecedented opportunities for the company to invest in its core businesses, with the outlook for the overall industries described as positive
- Continual growth in this sector in India is seen as necessary to support the industry, and the company says it is making all effort to accelerate the growth of its business
- Stated demand opportunities: vast industrial presence in both public and private sectors, huge demand for domestic services, availability of low-cost skilled human resources, and continued government thrust on reforms and further liberalisation
- Price is the deciding factor in most client decisions, alongside product quality, brand value and distribution network - a margin constraint management explicitly acknowledges

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Robotics hardware EBITDA margin ~20-25%; AMC + AI/software EBITDA margin ~30% — both well above AV. Margin expansion is purely a **mix-shift** story toward robotics/AI/software.
- FY26 blended EBITDA margin 16.4% (FY25 12.5%); H2 17.3%. Guidance +2-3 pts in FY27.
- R&D moving into TRN (~INR2-3 cr) said not to dent margins (already planned).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- IPO ~INR31.39 cr raised (Dec-2025 SME listing); ~99.5% deployed per objects, ~INR15-20 lakh pending.
- Debt ~INR4 cr (up from ~INR0.5 cr) — majority promoter loans, plus one bank loan @9.5% / 8-yr.
- RSVP Infotech bolt-on ~INR0.98 cr (Mar-2026). No dividend mentioned (recently listed micro-cap reinvesting).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion in this year was corporate and footprint-led rather than plant-led. The Company completed its Initial Public Offer, allotting 14,46,000 equity shares at Rs. 220 per share on 29th December 2025 under a shareholder authorisation for an issue of up to Rs. 50 Crore, and the Chairman describes the year as one in which the company transitioned from blueprint to reality, delivering on the strategic promises made following the IPO. Subsequent to the year end, the Company reported that development of its flagship Experience Center was near-complete, and it set up two new entities to extend reach and capability: Nanta Technologies FZ-LLC in the UAE, incorporated on April 23, 2026 to drive GCC market entry, and TRN India Private Limited, incorporated on April 24, 2026 to strengthen R&D in robotics and automation. No manufacturing capacity, plant or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in this material; the capital-commitments note supplied here carries the caption 'Estimated Amount of Contracts Remaining to be Executed on Capital Account and not Provided for' but no attributable figure or period.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - MD candid and accessible (16 yrs AV/IT background; ex-TE Connectivity, Kramer Electronics). Answered margin, WC, sourcing, acquisition-cost questions directly. Tone is confident-promotional, typical of a freshly-listed SME founder; heavy use of "we are seeing lots of trends." Guidance is broad-brush (40-50% growth, +2-3% margin) without granular bridges; the convergence/TAM framing ($107bn global service robotics by 2030) is top-down. No CFO/independent voice on the call — a quality/oversight gap to monitor.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Comprehensive, end-to-end AV integration offering spanning system design, integration and management and on-site support, so a single vendor covers the full deployment
- Breadth of the distributed AV product range - LED screens, professional displays, digital signage, digital podiums, video conferencing and UC devices plus accessories
- Proprietary AI platforms NTalk and NTRA launched during the year, and a branded service-robot line (Albotix) with over 400 robots sold
- Management states that experience in this business and quality assurance are the basis for overcoming competition, and that there are not enough competitors offering services like theirs

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Not a manufacturer:** robots OEM-contracted in India + imported from China → margin/supply/FX/tariff & differentiation risk; "proprietary" IP still nascent (TRN just formed).
- **Working capital / receivables stretch:** AV-SITC billing only on commissioning; project cycles slip on client side; receivables spike each H2. Mgmt says no sticky debtors but it's a structural drag.
- **H2 concentration / lumpiness:** revenue heavily back-ended to Q3/Q4 (project deliveries) — quarterly volatility.
- **Geographic concentration:** heavy Gujarat reliance; diversification (metros + UAE) just starting.
- **Single-voice, micro-cap SME:** only the MD on the call; low float/liquidity; aggressive ~50% growth + margin guidance hard to verify; some OCR/number inconsistencies in the transcript.
- **Promoter-funded debt** rising; governance/related-party watch.
- **Execution on RSVP/UAE/TRN** all unproven (FY27 contributions are projections).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The entire margin and re-rating story rests on a **mix-shift, not a manufacturing edge** — Nanta buys robots (India OEM + China imports) and wraps them in software/integration; durable advantage depends on TRN actually building proprietary product, which has barely started.
- The eye-catching "EBITDA INR84 crores" in H2 is an OCR/transcript error; real figure ~INR8.4 cr (17.3% of INR48.6 cr) — don't propagate the headline.
- RSVP Infotech (INR0.98 cr) is positioned to add INR15-20 cr revenue in FY27 — a ~15-20x revenue-to-cost ambition that is the single biggest swing factor in the ~50% growth guide; verify next quarter.
- Receivables/WC are the real risk, not demand: INR35 cr of H2's INR48 cr already collected, so cash conversion is okay so far, but the AV-SITC commissioning lag structurally inflates the balance sheet each H2.
- This is a sub-INR100 cr revenue, ~INR300 cr-mcap BSE-SME — interesting as a thematic India-robotics/AI-adoption proxy, but liquidity, disclosure depth, and founder-only governance make it speculative.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Improve its position in the market by focusing on the technologically advanced and more profitable product and market segments
- Work aggressively in the areas of productivity, efficiency and cost reduction
- Invest significantly in each of its core businesses, with several developmental activities planned for the next fiscal year
- Compete on quality of services, reputation and client relationships rather than on price, against both organised and unorganised players

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)
challenges.body:
> Only challenges Nanta specifically discussed on this call. ✅=covered here, ⭐=sector-knowledge.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Robots are "imported directly from China" + "third-party OEMs in India" — Nanta does not manufacture | Indian robotics/automation OEMs & contract manufacturers who localise (sector-knowledge ⭐ — no clean listed pure-play named) | Nanta itself (margin/IP captured by suppliers, not Nanta) ✅; localisation also pressures Chinese imports | Picks-and-shovels value accrues to the actual makers; Nanta is a reseller/integrator until TRN builds IP — Med (structural), Low (no specific listed name to map) |
| AV project working-capital / billing-lag drag — "can't raise invoice until commissioning" on large civil/MEP/AV projects | Pure software/AI & service-robotics models with B2C-like, lower-WC economics (incl. Nanta's own pivot) ✅ | Project-based AV/SITC integrators (incl. Nanta's AV vertical) ✅ | Mgmt explicitly pivoting to robotics/AI to cut WC days — Med |
| GCC/global robotics+AV market "fairly competitive with global players" | Global robotics/AV majors with scale (foreign ⭐ — not Indian-listed) | Sub-scale new entrants like Nanta unless differentiation holds | End-to-end solution claim is the only moat vs entrenched peers — Low (early, unproven) |
| BFSI demand for AI automation (Pointer Insurance INR6.6 cr win) | Listed Indian IT/AI-automation & insurtech-enabling vendors (sector-knowledge ⭐ — e.g. mid-cap IT services) | Manual/legacy back-office processes | One small order ≠ trend yet; signals BFSI AI-automation pull broadly — Low |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **H2 FY26 / Q4 FY26 (this — first call post Dec-2025 SME IPO):** FY26 revenue INR70.1 cr (+36.8%); H2 revenue INR48.6 cr (+52.2%); FY26 PAT INR8.2 cr (+70.5%), margin 11.7%; FY26 EBITDA INR11.5 cr (+78.8%), margin 16.4%; Robotics & AI ~36-37% of revenue; ~400 robots sold; RSVP Infotech acquired (~INR0.98 cr, Mar-26); TRN (51%) and UAE FZ LLC incorporated; Pointer Insurance INR6.6 cr AI order; ~INR31.4 cr IPO ~99.5% deployed.
- _Next H/Q → check: (1) Robotics+AI mix actually toward 60-65%? (2) FY27 revenue ~50% & EBITDA +2-3 pts? (3) RSVP delivering INR15-20 cr? (4) UAE revenue from Q2 (~INR30 cr FY27 target) and FZ LLC traction; (5) working-capital/receivable days trending down; (6) dealers 4→15; (7) Experience Center live; (8) TRN R&D INR2-3 cr & any proprietary product launch; (9) confirm the H2 EBITDA = ~INR8.4 cr (fix OCR); (10) promoter-debt level._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] RSVP Infotech acquired during FY26, adding 14 AI engineers and strengthening AI/software capabilities, the Allbotix platform architecture, and enterprise engagement capabilities for larger automation deployments.
- [Corporate history] Nanta Tech Limited incorporated June 2023; acquired the business of proprietorship-founded (2018) MNT Technologies on a going-concern basis in February 2024; listed on the BSE SME platform in December 2025.
- [Market tailwinds cited by company] Indian robotics market sized at $1.98bn (2025) growing to a projected $7.38bn (2034P); India ranked 6th globally in robot installations with cited 32x headroom versus China at similar population; robot component prices cited as down ~60% between 2022-2025, improving deployment ROI; Indian robotics startup funding cited as growing from $28.8M (2022) to $117M (2024).
